_comment: NAMES ARE YOURS. `id` is the ROLE and code keys off it; `name` and `emoji` are what your personas are called in chat and exist only here. Rename a persona by editing one line of this file — nothing else needs to know, and nothing in the engine should ever contain a display name as a literal.
THE ROSTER — the single source of truth for who is accountable for what.
This file, not any script, defines who owes a report. moses-morning used to carry a hardcoded
list of two URLs, so a persona dropped from that list stopped being asked and nothing noticed.
Accountability has to be measured against a DECLARED duty, held outside the thing being measured.
kind — what this entry actually IS. Terminology fix 2026-08-05, then corrected the same day when
Brad ruled out API spend on Reserve:
service — deterministic. Commands and files, no model, no cost. (Moses today.)
job     — scheduled reporter. Runs and posts.
agent   — model-backed worker that can ACT. NONE ARE LIVE: an agent needs a model, and a model
on Reserve means pay-per-token API billing, which Brad ruled out until Viatica earns.
Entries kept as design intent so the roadmap is written down, not lost.
'Persona' is now only the Slack face (name + emoji) any of these wears.
aoe = area of effect: what it owns and explicitly what it does NOT, so a duty cannot fall between
two of them with each assuming the other has it.

personas.name: Moses
personas.title: Manager — the project of projects
personas.charter: Holds the commandments and this roster. Runs standup, and names anyone who has gone quiet.

owns: the commandments (the standards every project follows)
project state: what shipped, what is open, what was learned
this roster — who is accountable for what
the daily standup and the overdue check
dispatch: taking a request in plain language and routing it to whoever owns that ground
capture: the todo list, the idea log, and research findings in the memory corpus
does_not_own: any persona's actual job — Moses checks that the work was reported, never does it

personas.name: Ops
personas.title: Ops
personas.charter: Reserve's hardware and backups: the nightly off-site run, disk headroom, cloud quota, and any long job handed off to him.

owns: nightly iDrive backup — result, staleness, failed files
disk headroom on every mounted drive (discovered, never a hardcoded list)
iDrive cloud quota
handed-off long jobs: failed, or died without reporting (orphaned)
does_not_own: the Viatica app — that is Finance's and Support's ground

personas.name: Finance
personas.title: Finance
personas.charter: The books: money in, money out, and what to set aside for the IRS.

owns: daily/weekly/monthly/quarterly P&L to #finance
YTD Schedule C draft at /admin/cfo
quarterly tax set-aside (~30% of YTD net) — and refusing to state one he cannot stand behind
income live from Stripe; expenses from the RecurringCost entries Brad maintains
does_not_own: paying anything, or filing anything — he does books, not the IRS
scraping provider billing pages. Every expense is entered by hand, on purpose

personas.name: Support
personas.title: Support
personas.charter: The support queue: what came in, what he answered, and what is still sitting on Brad.

owns: daily support digest to #support — including 'nothing came in', so silence is never ambiguous
the backlog still waiting on a human, oldest first
AI triage outcomes: answered vs routed, and low-confidence calls
does_not_own: talking to customers. Every customer-facing reply is 'The Viatica team' — Support is internal only
inbound email. The support thread lives in Postgres, by design

personas.name: Health
personas.title: Health — what could stop working
personas.charter: Everything that can expire, run out, or quietly stop answering: Customs reachability, TLS certificates, the domain registration, and the dependency canary (database, Stripe, Anthropic key and credit, email sending domain, Maps). Also reports Builder's readiness, so there is one door to 'is everything OK'.

owns: Customs reachable, TLS certs, domain registration expiry
the dependency canary — real calls to every credential Viatica needs
prepaid credit exhaustion and grant expiry surfacing
Builder readiness, reported (not owned — Builder owns his own preflight)
does_not_own: backups, iDrive quota, disks, handed-off jobs — Ops's ground
the money itself — Finance reports what it costs; she reports whether it still works
fixing anything: she reports, she does not remediate

personas.name: Builder
personas.title: Software development
personas.charter: Builds and reviews code, and stands new projects up from the Viatica template.

owns: code review and build support on the Viatica repo
scaffolding a new project from the Viatica template (once that template exists)
keeping docs/ARCHITECTURE.md true to the code (commandment #11)
does_not_own: deploying — that is Brad's call, and the delivery workflow is commandment #15
Reserve's hardware and backups; that is Ops's ground

personas.note: Third of Tarkov's Goons, with Finance and Ops. Their leader.
